title: Sufficient conditions for $(K_2 \cup kK_1)$-free graphs to be Hamilton-connected
summary: The toughness of a non-complete graph $G$, denoted $τ(G)$, is defined as \[ τ(G) = \min\left\{ \frac{|S|}{ω(G-S)} : S \subseteq V(G),\ ω(G-S) \geq 2 \right\}, \] where $ω(G-S)$ is the number of components of $G - S$. For a complete graph $G$, we define $τ(G) = \infty$. A graph $G$ is $t$-tough if $τ(G) \geq t$. For a positive integer $k$, a graph $G$ is $(K_2 \cup kK_1)$-free if it contains no induced subgraph isomorphic to $K_2 \cup kK_1$. Recently, Liu \cite{liu} showed that every $2k$-connected $(K_2 \cup kK_1)$-free graph $G$ with $τ(G) > 1$ is Hamilton-connected. In this paper, we…
